title: Ulyana and the Summer
premise: Quentin Okonkwo, who publishes her novels under the name 'Ulyana Vale,' has spent twelve years on a remote island keeping grief at arm's length after the drowning of her first love, Sasha. When a letter Sasha mailed the week he died finally surfaces in a flooded post office archive, it pulls her back into the summer she buried — and into the orbit of Marisol Reyes, the marine archivist hired to catalog the island's records, who has secrets of her own about why she really came. As Quentin and Marisol grow close, the letter's contents reveal that Sasha's death was not an accident and that someone powerful on the mainland profited from covering it up. Quentin must choose between the safe, small life she built and exposing the truth, learning to give her whole heart before the last ferry of the season strands them all for winter; the novel ends with the cover-up exposed, Marisol choosing to stay past the last ferry, and Quentin signing her new book with her real name at last.
about_author: Jonah Pemberton is the pen name of a former ferry deckhand who spent six summers crossing coastal waters before turning to writing full-time. They live in a drafty house near a working lighthouse and claim the sea still dictates their deadlines.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Quentin's POV. Quentin tends the automated lighthouse her grandfather once kept, writes romance novels as 'Ulyana Vale,' and measures her days in small safe rituals. A storm knocks out the island's power, and among salvaged boxes from the old post office she glimpses an envelope with handwriting she'd know anywhere. Beat: comfort disrupted by a ghost.

chapters.title: Postmarked Eleven Years Ago
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The letter is from Sasha, dated the week he drowned, never delivered. She can't bring herself to open it and locks it in the lighthouse desk. The mainland sends word that an archivist is coming to catalog the flood-damaged postal records. Beat: dread wrapped in denial.

chapters.title: The Woman from the Archive
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV introduced. Marisol Reyes arrives on the supply boat, brisk and observant, asking careful questions about the flooded records. Quentin resents her intrusion into the island's sediment of grief. Their first exchange is prickly, electric. Beat: friction as attraction's disguise.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Marisol catalogs waterlogged letters; Quentin watches her handle other people's grief with unexpected tenderness. Marisol mentions, too casually, that she requested this posting specifically. Quentin notices but files it away. Beat: curiosity kindling.

chapters.title: Unopened
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A sleepless night ends with Quentin holding Sasha's letter over a candle flame, unable to burn or open it. Flashback threads to the summer twelve years ago: Sasha's laugh, the boat, the storm. Beat: the past pressing its palm flat against the present.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol finds Quentin swimming at dawn — the first time anyone has seen her in the water since the drowning. They share coffee in the lighthouse; Marisol lies lightly about her reasons for coming, and hates herself for it. Beat: intimacy built on a fault line.

chapters.title: The Ferry Schedule
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The last ferry of the season is announced for six weeks out. Quentin realizes whatever happens with Marisol has a deadline, which suits her habit of lending pieces of herself rather than risking the whole. They fall into a rhythm of evenings. Beat: happiness with an hourglass inside it.

chapters.title: Sasha's Last Summer
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, deep flashback chapter. Twelve years ago: Sasha worked for the Calloway family's mainland shipping firm, came back changed, talked about 'things that have to come out.' Then the storm, the empty boat, the verdict of accident. Beat: the wound reopened in full color.

chapters.title: A Letter, Read
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol discovers a duplicate of Sasha's letter in the damaged archive — opened, logged, then deliberately misfiled eleven years ago by someone with authority. She now knows the death was investigated and buried. She says nothing to Quentin. Beat: knowledge as burden.

chapters.title: Pieces Lent, Pieces Kept
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. First kiss, in the lighthouse gallery at dusk. Quentin offers Marisol a version of herself carefully edited — no Sasha, no grief, no letter. Marisol accepts the edited version and feels the lie like a stone in her pocket. Beat: tenderness shadowed by concealment.

chapters.title: The Calloway Name
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol traces the misfiled letter to a signature: Edmund Calloway, now a shipping magnate — and the man whose firm employed Sasha. Her own secret surfaces to the reader: her father was the investigating officer forced off the case, ruined for asking questions. Beat: the stakes sharpen into something personal.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A gale traps both women in the lighthouse overnight. Power fails; by lamplight, walls come down. Marisol nearly tells Quentin everything; instead she asks what happened to Sasha, and Quentin, for the first time, speaks his name aloud. Beat: confession almost arriving.

chapters.title: What Sasha Wrote
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Quentin finally opens the letter. Sasha wrote that he'd found evidence Calloway's ships were running contraband through the island, that if anything happened to him it wasn't the weather. Quentin's twelve-year architecture of 'accident' collapses. Beat: devastation as liberation.

chapters.title: The Whole Heart
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Shaken, Quentin gives Marisol the unedited self — the letter, the guilt, the years of small safe steps. But she catches Marisol's flicker of recognition and realizes Marisol already knew something. Trust cracks precisely where it had just deepened. Beat: honesty met with suspicion.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Archive
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Quentin demands the truth; Marisol reveals her father's ruin and the misfiled duplicate. Rage, then reluctant alliance: two people who each protected the other from a truth neither could carry alone. Beat: rupture becoming partnership.

chapters.title: Evidence in Salt Water
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The pair reconstructs the cover-up: Sasha's evidence log, a bribed harbormaster, Calloway's men on the island the night he died. Someone on the mainland learns Marisol has been asking questions. Beat: rising tension, the hunt turned around.

chapters.title: Visitors
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Two well-dressed men arrive on the supply run, asking about 'archival irregularities.' The islanders close ranks around Quentin — belonging shown, not stated. Marisol hides the recovered evidence in the lighthouse. Beat: community as fortress.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry Approaches
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. With three days until the final sailing, Marisol must choose: leave with the evidence and her father's vindication handled safely ashore, or stay through the winter beside Quentin. She hasn't answered Quentin's unspoken question. Beat: the choice crystallizing.

chapters.title: Calloway Comes to the Island
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Edmund Calloway himself arrives, offering Quentin money and silence, revealing he knew who she was all along. Quentin refuses — not bravely, but tremblingly, which makes it braver. He threatens to make the island pay. Beat: power showing its corruption face-to-face.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Ferry
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Calloway's men attempt to burn the archive shed; the islanders and the two women save the evidence in a chaotic firelight battle. Marisol is injured shielding the letter. In the aftermath, Quentin realizes she cannot let Marisol leave — or let fear decide anything ever again. Beat: climax's threshold.

chapters.title: Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. At the dock, the evidence goes aboard with a trusted journalist and Marisol's sworn statement — but Marisol stays, missing the boat deliberately, choosing Quentin and the island's long winter. They kiss as the ferry pulls away carrying the truth toward daylight. Beat: the whole heart, risked and kept.

chapters.title: Signed with My Own Name
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, epilogue in early spring. Calloway is indicted; her father's name cleared alongside Marisol's. Quentin finishes her new novel and, for the first time, publishes under Quentin Okonkwo — no more Ulyana, no more hiding. On the lighthouse gallery, the season's first ferry returns. Beat: survival's price paid, belonging earned, love signed in full.
